scientificAccuracy.notes: Science as in assessment_conducting-experiments__r1: a good hypothesis is a testable, educated guess that explains a cause-and-effect relationship; independent, dependent, and control variables in new experiments; quantitative versus qualitative observations; observations versus inferences; fair-test controls.

standardAndLearningTargetPreserved.notes: Same practice standards and learning goals as assessment_conducting-experiments__r1; bound to canonical r1 (no canonical r2).

cognitiveDemandPreserved.notes: Same reasoning per item in adapted language; three displayed choices per item is the accepted reading-adapted accommodation profile (adapted language, choiceCount 3).

correctAnswerEquivalence.notes: The canonical correct option is displayed on every item and each adapted correct choice keeps the canonical r1 correct meaning.

distractorMisconceptionEquivalence.notes: Retained distractors keep the diagnostic misconceptions recorded in the authoring notes, including the IV/DV swaps in q2 and q6 and the observation/inference reversal in q5; q1 keeps the unsupported-guess and proven-fact misconceptions.

omittedDistractorAppropriate.notes: Each item omits exactly one canonical distractor with a recorded rationale, approved as presented, including the q1 omission of D and the q10 removal of the near-duplicate independent-variable lure.

noAnswerCueing.notes: Local automated review: 0 hard findings and 0 warnings as displayed; display positions BACCABACBA (A4 B3 C3); the correct choice is uniquely longest on 1 of 10 items (canonical 8 of 10). The 10 strings kept identical to canonical have recorded reasons.

showYourThinkingEquivalence.notes: Adapted prompt and structured paragraph model (Claim:, Evidence:, Reasoning: leads and the closing paragraph) keep the claim-evidence-reasoning demand; semantic required terms claim, evidence, reasoning. The canonical Mentos supplied evidence (ce-data) is locked and identical, and every measurement the adapted model cites is a supplied trial height of the soda it names. Accepted presentation details: the prompt bolds each term with its colon outside the emphasis, and the model does not italicize which and why.

explanationEquivalence.notes: Adapted feedback preserves the meaning of each canonical r1 explanation.

items.notes: Owner approved: displays A (hypothesis as an unsupported guess), B (correct), C (hypothesis as a proven fact); D (the starting question) intentionally omitted.
